text: {"observations":"Broadband noise fills the whole clip up to the ~5.6 kHz cutoff, strongest below ~1 kHz, and is not steady: it is loud from 0-1.6 s, drops abruptly at ~1.6 s, then swells again later. Voiced speech harmonics (curved contours at ~2-3.5 s, 4.3-6 s and ~9 s) sit on top of it, suggesting people talking outdoors. Gusty, fluctuating, low-frequency-weighted noise fits wind on a microphone better than the steady hiss of rain (C), and such persistent noise rules out calm (B) and quiet snow (D). The choice between wind and rain is uncertain; A is the best fit.","answer":"A"}
